claim: the label reads Wine of Origin Estate
because: Estate is no longer a Wine of Origin unit or designation of geographic origin. Current rules allow only the production term "estate wine", for wine whose grapes were grown, made and bottled on the same registered unit. The change came with the revision of the scheme usually dated to 2004. The keyed answer is still right, but a current Cape label cannot read "Wine of Origin Estate".
fix: Stem: "A visitor buys a bottle at a cellar door and the label reads Estate Wine. What has that term committed the producer to?" Explanation, first sentence: "Estate wine must come from units registered for estate production, so the claim is that the grapes were grown and the wine made and bottled in the same place; since the 2004 revision estate is no longer a unit of origin in its own right."
